Hi Chloe, good to meet you. Sorry to hear you're dealing with this again. I want to ask a few questions to make sure we treat the right thing.

1. When you say burning when you wee — is the burning only as you pass urine, or is it there all the time?
2. Are you needing to go more often than usual, or rushing to get there?
3. Have you noticed any blood in your urine?
4. Any fever, chills or feeling generally unwell?
5. Any pain in your lower back or sides?
6. Any unusual vaginal discharge, itching or irritation down there?
reply: The burning is only when I pass urine, worst at the end. I'm going more often than usual and rushing to get there. No blood in my urine, just a bit cloudy and smells. No fever or shivers, I feel fine apart from this. No pain in my back, just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy. No discharge, itching or irritation.

awards.label: Colour of the urine or any visible blood
Red flag excluded: Fever, sweats, chills or shaking
Red flag excluded: Pain in the back or sides (loins)

utterance:
Here's where we're at, Chloe:

Your urine test today confirms a bladder infection (cystitis) — it showed white cells and bacteria markers. The good news is everything else points to a simple infection in the bladder only: your temperature is normal, you feel well, and there's no kidney tenderness, so this isn't a kidney infection.

I'm giving you nitrofurantoin — a different antibiotic from last time, because the ones you took a couple of weeks ago for your cold can make bladder bugs resistant to the usual first choice. Take one 100 mg capsule four times a day for 5 days, with food to reduce the chance of nausea. A couple of points on that:

- Your antibiotic doesn't affect your contraceptive pill, so it stays reliable — but since you missed some pills recently, if you're having sex in the next week, it's worth using condoms as well.
- About the antibiotics for your cold — colds are viruses, and antibiotics don't help them; they just increase the chance of bugs becoming resistant, like what may have happened here. Worth keeping in mind next time.

What to expect and do:
- The burning should improve within 1-2 days. Drink plenty of water, and don't hold on for long when you need to go.
- The lab culture result and your chlamydia screen take about 2 days. If the bug turns out to be resistant to nitrofurantoin, or if chlamydia comes back positive, we'll contact you to change or add treatment. If you haven't heard from us by the end of the week, please call the clinic.
- You're getting these infections fairly often now — two in a few months. If you get a third within a year, come back and we'll talk about prevention strategies (like emptying your bladder after sex and daily prevention options).

Please come back or seek urgent care straight away if you get: fever or shivering episodes, vomiting, one-sided back or loin pain, or if you're feeling worse rather than better after 48 hours on the antibiotics. Those would suggest the infection has moved up to the kidney, which needs different treatment.

Any questions for me?
reply: Thanks, that makes sense. I'll take the antibiotics as prescribed and try to drink more water. I'll keep an eye on how I feel and call if anything changes. I guess I'll just keep doing what I can to stay on top of it.

quotes.acceptable_2: Take one 100 mg capsule four times a day for 5 days, with food to reduce the chance of nausea.
